knowledge:
- key_parameters: reference_path=The directory where the SpliceWiz reference is built and stored ;; fasta=Path to the genome FASTA file or AnnotationHub record ID ;; gtf=Path to the gene annotation GTF file or AnnotationHub record ID ;; genome_type=Specifies pre-built mappability exclusions (accepts "hg38", "hg19", "mm10", "mm9") ;; ontologySpecies=Species name to generate gene ontology annotations ;; bamfiles=Character vector of paths to alignment BAM files ;; sample_names=Character vector of unique sample names corresponding to BAM files ;; output_path=Directory where processBAM or collateData outputs are written ;; n_threads=Number of threads to use for multi-threaded operations ;; Experiment=A 2- or 3-column data frame containing sample names and processed file paths ;; novelSplicing=Logical indicating whether to enable novel splicing detection ;; IRMode=Method to determine total spliced transcript abundance ("SpliceOver" or "SpliceMax") ;; lowMemoryMode=Logical to minimize RAM usage during collation at the cost of speed ;; realize=Logical to load all data into memory at construction of the NxtSE object ;; RemoveOverlapping=Logical to remove overlapping introns belonging to minor isoforms ;; test_factor=The colData column name representing the experimental condition ;; test_nom=The numerator condition level for pairwise contrast ;; test_denom=The denominator condition level for pairwise contrast ;; IRmode=Method to quantify intron retention in differential analysis ("all", "annotated", or "annotated_binary")
- alternatives: ASE_DoubleExpSeq=Uses DoubleExpSeq (beta-binomial model); preferred for quick pairwise comparisons without batch factors ;; ASE_limma=Uses limma (log-normal model); fastest method, ideal for large datasets and supports time-series ;; ASE_edgeR=Uses edgeR (quasi-likelihood negative binomial); recommended for final analysis with batch correction and time-series, deals well with near-zero counts ;; ASE_DESeq=Uses DESeq2 (negative binomial); most computationally expensive but highly robust, supports batch correction and time-series
- when_to_use: Use when performing alternative splicing analysis (including skipped exons, mutually exclusive exons, alternative splice sites, and intron retention) from RNA-seq BAM files, especially when dealing with large datasets requiring multi-threaded processing and interactive visualization.
- pitfalls: High memory usage during collateData (can use 6-7 GB per thread; use lowMemoryMode=TRUE to limit to ~8 GB) ;; Over-calling intron retention due to overlapping introns (mitigated by default RemoveOverlapping=TRUE in makeSE) ;; MacOS users without OpenMP libraries will experience high RAM usage (5-10 GB per BAM) due to fallback multi-threading (install libomp via brew to resolve) ;; Conda environments using r-base=4.3 may fail (r-base=4.2.1 is recommended)

workflows.name: standard_alternative_splicing_analysis
workflows.intent: Build a reference, process alignment BAM files, collate sample data, filter low-confidence events, and perform differential alternative splicing analysis.
workflows.stages: 1. Build the SpliceWiz reference using buildRef() ;; 2. Process BAM files to extract junction and intron coverage data using processBAM() ;; 3. Collate processed sample outputs into an experiment database using collateData() ;; 4. Import the collated experiment as an NxtSE object using makeSE() ;; 5. Filter out low-confidence alternative splicing events using applyFilters() ;; 6. Perform differential alternative splicing analysis using ASE_edgeR() (or other statistical wrappers)
workflows.code:
ref_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "Reference" )
buildRef ( reference_path = ref_path, fasta = chrZ_genome (), gtf = chrZ_gtf (), ontologySpecies = "Homo sapiens" )
bams <- SpliceWiz_example_bams ()
bams <- findBAMS ( tempdir (), level = 0 )
pb_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "pb_output" )
processBAM ( bamfiles = bams $ path, sample_names = bams $ sample, reference_path = ref_path, output_path = pb_path )
expr <- findSpliceWizOutput (pb_path)
nxtse_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "NxtSE_output" )
collateData ( Experiment = expr, reference_path = ref_path, output_path = nxtse_path )
se <- makeSE (nxtse_path)
se <- realize_NxtSE (se)
colData (se) $ condition <- rep ( c ( "A" , "B" ), each = 3 )
colData (se) $ batch <- rep ( c ( "K" , "L" , "M" ), 2 )
se.filtered <- se[ applyFilters (se),]
require ( "edgeR" )
res_edgeR <- ASE_edgeR ( se = se.filtered, test_factor = "condition" , test_nom = "B" , test_denom = "A" )
<<<ENDWORKFLOW

workflows.name: novel_splicing_detection
workflows.intent: Detect and analyze novel alternative splicing events using unannotated junctions and tandem reads.
workflows.stages: 1. Build the SpliceWiz reference using buildRef() ;; 2. Process BAM files using processBAM() ;; 3. Collate data with novel splicing detection enabled using collateData() ;; 4. Import the collated experiment as an NxtSE object using makeSE() ;; 5. Filter and perform differential alternative splicing analysis
workflows.code:
ref_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "Reference" )
buildRef ( reference_path = ref_path, fasta = chrZ_genome (), gtf = chrZ_gtf (), ontologySpecies = "Homo sapiens" )
bams <- SpliceWiz_example_bams ()
bams <- findBAMS ( tempdir (), level = 0 )
pb_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "pb_output" )
processBAM ( bamfiles = bams $ path, sample_names = bams $ sample, reference_path = ref_path, output_path = pb_path )
expr <- findSpliceWizOutput (pb_path)
nxtse_path <- file.path ( tempdir (), "NxtSE_output_novel" )
collateData ( Experiment = expr, reference_path = ref_path, output_path = nxtse_path, novelSplicing = TRUE , novelSplicing_requireOneAnnotatedSJ = TRUE , novelSplicing_minSamples = 3 , novelSplicing_minSamplesAboveThreshold = 1 , novelSplicing_countThreshold = 10 , novelSplicing_useTJ = TRUE )
se <- makeSE (nxtse_path)
se.filtered <- se[ applyFilters (se),]
require ( "edgeR" )
res_edgeR <- ASE_edgeR ( se = se.filtered, test_factor = "condition" , test_nom = "B" , test_denom = "A" )
<<<ENDWORKFLOW

workflows.name: star_alignment_and_reference_generation
workflows.intent: Build a STAR genome index and align FASTQ files to generate BAMs using SpliceWiz wrappers.
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare genome resources using getResources() ;; 2. Build a STAR genome reference using STAR_BuildRef() ;; 3. Align FASTQ files using STAR_alignExperiment()
workflows.code:
ref_path = "./Reference"
if ( ! dir.exists ( file.path (ref_path, "resource" ))) { getResources ( reference_path = ref_path, fasta = "genome.fa" , gtf = "transcripts.gtf" ) }
STAR_BuildRef ( reference_path = ref_path, n_threads = 8 )
Experiment <- data.frame ( sample = c ( "sample_A" , "sample_B" ), forward = file.path ( "raw_data" , c ( "sample_A" , "sample_B" ), c ( "sample_A_1.fastq" , "sample_B_1.fastq" )), reverse = file.path ( "raw_data" , c ( "sample_A" , "sample_B" ), c ( "sample_A_2.fastq" , "sample_B_2.fastq" )) )
STAR_alignExperiment ( Experiment = Experiment, STAR_ref_path = file.path ( "Reference_FTP" , "STAR" ), BAM_output_path = "./bams" , n_threads = 8 , two_pass = FALSE )
<<<ENDWORKFLOW
